item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russian drones have struck Ukrainian rail infrastructure, killing 13 at one station and 14 on a platform in Dnipro, while night attacks have left 350,000 people without power in the same city. Ukrainian investigators have concluded that Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians, and the EU has freed over 20 billion euros to potentially help Ukraine's defence. Germany and Ukraine are testing an armed ground robot for frontline deployment, and US pressure has led Ukraine to pause strikes on Russian oil refineries. Trump officials are discussing sanctions relief for a Russian fund, and a localized ceasefire in Oleshky has entered its third day. The conflict has caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
JD Vance has sent a letter to Iran's president urging a restart of peace talks while Qatar has called on Iran to end regional threats and reopen the Strait of Hormuz as a goodwill gesture. The IRGC reports that four tankers were struck by mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's covert military network is moving hardware past the U.S. blockade. A top U.S. admiral briefed President Trump on possible attack options against Iran and the Pentagon dismissed a general accused of leaking classified information. An IDF soldier has been charged with spying for Iran in exchange for cryptocurrency, and oil prices have eased as the United States seeks renewed diplomacy with Iran. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Yemen and the Red Sea: the situation
item.description:
Houthi forces have stepped up attacks, striking Saudi airports and oil facilities and launching missiles toward Riyadh and the Ras Tanura refinery, while Saudi air defenses intercepted missiles over the Eastern Province. The coalition responded with airstrikes that hit a market in northern Yemen and a petrol station, causing civilian casualties, and a Saudi strike killed 12 people in a residential area. Fighting continues near Yemen’s Taiz as the UN urges humanitarian access. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Syria: the situation
item.description:
Jordan resumed airstrikes in southern Syria targeting Daesh, prompting Syrian condemnation and reports of civilian casualties, while a joint security committee and investigation into the strikes were agreed between the two states and the Nasib border crossing reopened. Syrian security forces killed a French jihadist in Harem and another French fighter in Idlib, and unidentified gunmen killed two Syrian defence ministry personnel in Idlib. Heavy rain and flash floods across Syria killed five people, including four children. Syria announced the release of 57 prisoners transferred from Lebanon and joined an Arab anti-drug conference in Tunisia to boost regional cooperation. The UCDP recorded 2,732 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Iraqi security agencies arrested nine suspects on human-trafficking charges and a parliamentarian was sentenced for illegal oil contracts. The Kurdistan region deepened security coordination with Baghdad and advanced weapons-control measures. 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

In the Upper Nile region, fighting since March 2025 has displaced 125,000 people and killed 180, prompting a UN envoy to call for consensus among leaders. Opposition leader Machar continues to dispute Bol Mel’s claims over the Nasir attack, while Odinga has appealed for international intervention after meeting President Kiir. item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Russian Su-35 fighter jets and S-400 air defence systems have arrived in Ethiopia as fighting spreads across Tigray, Amhara and Oromia, with drone strikes hitting an IDP camp in Amhara and a shelter in South Wollo, causing civilian casualties. Militant attackers killed at least 60 Orthodox Christians in Oromia, while drone strikes in Amhara killed 14, including children. Thousands of people are fleeing the border clashes, with about 50,000 refugees arriving in Moyale, Kenya. The conflict has also seen Ethiopia begin homegrown drone manufacturing. The UCDP recorded 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Al Shabaab fighters are intensifying attacks on Turkish-trained Somali troops in Lower Shabelle and ambushing units near Baidoa, while Somali intelligence killed a former al-Shabaab finance chief in Lower Shabelle. African Union peacekeepers are withdrawing from four bases in Lower Shabelle and Ethiopia is pulling more than 3,000 troops from Somalia amid fighting at home, reducing external military presence. The federal government has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF-17 fighter jets, the United States has imposed entry conditions on ships calling at Somali ports, and the UAE carried out its first drone strike against Al Shabaab in nearly a year. Piracy off Somalia’s coast is rising, with hijacked oil tankers and hostages reported, and the conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

In Niger, a convoy carrying Governor Bago collided with a car, killing four students, a driver and a young woman, and Niger accused Chad of a drone attack that killed two civilians. Algeria has deployed troops to Niger to protect energy assets, its first foreign mission in over 50 years. Militants now control at least 40% of Burkina Faso, a critic of Mali’s junta was forcibly disappeared, and the junta stripped five more exiled critics of nationality. The conflict produced 4,159 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have risen above 10,000, and a nurse treating patients was killed by a mob while another health worker was wounded. item.title: Israel and Hezbollah: the situation
item.description:
Hezbollah continues to fire rockets and artillery at Israeli positions in southern Lebanon while Israel carries out air strikes on Hezbollah sites, causing civilian casualties. In northern Israel a Hezbollah submunition exploded in a teenager's backpack, killing Elazar Yair Wilensky and wounding dozens, prompting an IDF investigation. Lebanese olive harvests proceed under the threat of drones and warplanes, and UN peacekeepers are withdrawing from Lebanon after pressure from Israel. Qatar has pledged reconstruction funding and announced a large solar plant project for southern Lebanon. The UCDP recorded 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
